text:
dan_arch: quick follow-up to the CP-split RFC. I'm proposing a 'locality boundary' layer that owns ephemeral egress leases, affinity, and a minimal cert bundle per region. CP remains the canonical metadata authority but punts src-ip preservation and NAT ownership to the boundary. TL;DR: reduce hairpin and make egress accounting region-local.

alex_m: can you sketch how this is different from relay vs peering?

dan_arch: ascii sketch:
```
global-cp
  |
  +-- region-A-boundary --> tenant-egress-pool-A (ENI/NAT) --> internet / customer-vpc
  |
  +-- region-B-boundary --> tenant-egress-pool-B
```
boundaries only handle L3/L4 egress and short-circuiting. relays still exist for full CP control flows.

priya_r: boundaries sound like thin operators. Do they terminate traffic or just perform NAT/affinity?

dan_arch: thin operators. They don't run the inference stacks. They manage ephemeral IP leases, route affinity, and the local certs/tokens used for short-lived authorization.

jamal_s: risk: if a boundary is compromised and has cert material, blast radius increases. How do we handle key material and rotation?

dan_arch: proposal: boundary keys are short-lived and KMS-wrapped. CP issues signed lease tokens with a TTL (default 10m). Boundaries renew via CP; if renewal fails, boundary serves existing leases until expiry and marks itself degraded. Nonce + anti-replay in lease tokens.

sara_ops: how does private-only (no internet) customers work?

dan_arch: boundary maps egress-pool to private endpoints (peering/privatelink). Behavior is identical: enforce policy but route to private backend instead of NAT. This keeps the same operator surface and rollout story.

alex_m: failure semantics? fail-open or fail-closed on CP partition?

dan_arch: recommend fail-soft: continue with active leases until TTL; disallow new leases while disconnected. Mark region in console and trigger remediation.

priya_r: any perf/cost numbers?

dan_arch: rough sim: for ~30% regional-local traffic, p95 improved ~20-25% and we avoid double-transit on many flows giving ~10-15% egress cost improvement. Needs load testing.

jamal_s: ops overhead: more endpoints to monitor/rotate. Centralized logging/metrics needed.

dan_arch: agreed. boundaries export metrics and lease events to CP logging pipeline (region-indexed). Auto-remediation playbook for cert mismatch/NAT exhaustion.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist v0.1: [boundary image], [lease protocol v2], [metrics export], [private-endpoint mapping], [cutover playbook].

sara_ops: rollout: feature-flag per-customer. start with dev tenants in region-A for 2 weeks, watch p95, egress bill, and NAT exhaustion.

alex_m: compatibility with Dedicated/Private?

dan_arch: Dedicated: boundary deployed inside customer VPC (sidecar-mode). Private/airgapped: boundary runs with stub CP sync over async connector. API and behavior consistent across modes.

priya_r: security checklist additions: least-priv IAM, KMS envelope separation, mTLS CP<->boundary, signed lease token, nonce anti-replay, cert rotation cadence.

jamal_s: add integration tests for route-flap during lease renewal to prevent src-ip flip mid-connection.

dan_arch: will add appendix to RFC: lease token format, TTL defaults, health signals, cutover playbook, rollout gates. Action items:
- dan_arch: update appendix + diagram (due EOD Friday)
- priya_r: security checklist (due Mon)
- jamal_s: NAT/route-flap test plan (due next Wed)
- sara_ops: rollout playbook draft (due next Fri)

alex_m: :thumbsup: small naming nit: use "locality boundary" in docs to avoid product confusion.

dan_arch: agreed. I'll push draft to RFC repo and ping arch review. thanks everyone.
